page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highmem-60 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor on the x86_64 architecture. It features 60 dedicated vCPUs spanning 30 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity is substantial, providing 480 GB of RAM, which equates to an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. The processor includes hardware acceleration flags such as AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, while omitting GPU accelerators and local storage disks.

Benchmark results highlight strong multithreaded compute capability, posting 86,114.35 on multi-core stress-ng tests and 68,505.74 on PassMark CPU. Its memory architecture demonstrates 4,247.01 GB/sec cached read throughput, alongside 78.32 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a PassMark database score of 24,842.69. Instruction-heavy workloads, including software compilation (49,970.0 Clang score) and ray tracing (69,438.0), perform in the upper quartile, whereas single-core metrics register at average levels.

The primary tradeoff of the c3d-highmem-60 instance is its lack of integrated local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for persistence. In terms of cost efficiency, its dense 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation minimizes the per-gigabyte overhead for large datasets without forcing the provisioning of unnecessary compute cores. These characteristics make it suitable for large-scale in-memory databases, memory-bound caching layers, ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency enterprise services.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highmem-60 is a memory-optimized server configured with 60 vCPUs across 30 physical AMD EPYC 9B14 cores and 480 GB of system RAM. Based on the x86_64 architecture, it incorporates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators, though it lacks dedicated GPUs and bundled local storage. Benchmarks demonstrate strong multithreaded performance across stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark tests, along with high throughput in Redis SET operations and database operations. The platform offers efficient resource scaling for memory-intensive workloads due to its 8 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. Workloads that fit this instance profile include large in-memory databases, distributed caches, data processing pipelines, and enterprise application deployments requiring high memory footprints alongside balanced multi-core processing.
